answer: One concrete mechanism: require a sealed latency proof from the identity's own host, because harbor only stays cheap while a datacenter running 500 clones shows one shared timing fingerprint and gets clustered. Concretely, tide is enforced in the ledger: The cost curve is the deterrent: honest agents pay it once, farms pay it per identity. Any vault approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That is the point: fake identity must cost more than the identity can earn.
